analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 316-317). It adds two rows for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY, which are default-on Qwen MTP scheduling and decode toggles read in libs/mlx-swift-lm MTPContractsV2.swift. Both are documented as 'Not forwarded to LaunchAgents', so they apply only to foreground, local and test processes.

What I examined: the two added rows and the surrounding configuration reference (base lines 487-597 and head lines 1-311). The patch changes no code, no attestation or App Attest policy, no coordinator wire contract and no cache encryption. The new rows do not touch the prefix-cache storage, TTL or HMAC lookup controls described in T-041, and they do not touch the endpoint-resumption, logout or worker semantics in TB-011 and T-053. The head text I received ends at line 311, so I could not see the added lines at 316-317 directly and relied on the patch excerpt. That excerpt is marked incomplete and truncated, so other doc changes in the PR may exist.

Security considerations: the toggles alter MTP speculation scheduling and the history and carry seeding, which is a performance/latency behaviour. They are environment-controlled by the local operator, who is already ADV-001 within TB-003, and they are not in the LaunchAgent passthrough allowlist. I found no new attack surface, no weakened mitigation and no invalidated assumption. The claimed effect on output correctness (ordinary decode versus hidden-returning seed steps) is defined by library code outside the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the code matches the documented semantics or that MTP output is unchanged, which is a general correctness question under T-007 and T-056 and not a regression shown here.
